issue.title: Muse agent keeps re-submitting the same accepted final declaration and re-noting its bead for 20 minutes in one provider turn

task_type_fields.impact:
- About 20 minutes of wasted provider usage and 380 redundant tool calls.
- A bead note log flooded with 22 duplicate entries, which every later reader (land agents, humans) must page through.
- Repeated live GitHub/PyPI probes.

The pattern recurs whenever a Muse phase agent cannot close its bead in-turn, which is exactly the "wait for landing / human gate / soak" case that SASE's single-turn contract says must end the turn (decision `single-turn-agents`).
task_type_fields.location: Muse provider turn termination after an accepted /sase_final declaration (src/sase/llm_provider Muse adapter / _subprocess_plain.py start_completion_watchdog)
task_type_fields.repro:
Observed once, on athena, run `sase-1my.6` (exit phase of epic sase-1my). It was a Muse runtime (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, provider `meta`, Muse session `db18d5d8-61c0-4c25-a553-84f4e99e97fe`). Its artifacts dir is `~/.sase/projects/gh_sase-org__sase/artifacts/ace-run/202610/19/20261019101833`.

- `final_submission_attempts.jsonl` holds **42 accepted submissions with one identical `submission_digest`**, recorded 2026-10-19T17:17:04Z–17:37:48Z. That is roughly one every 30 s for 20 minutes, all inside a single provider turn: `continuation_prompt_measurements.jsonl` has 1 row, and `tool_calls.jsonl` has 384 rows (374 Bash).
- Between declarations the model re-ran the same "is it closable yet?" probes and appended 22 near-identical "Dated recheck … Keeping IN_PROGRESS with bead_action keep" notes to bead `sase-1my.6` (notes #5–#26).
- The run's own final reply says "state is byte-identical to the recent dated rechecks, so no new bead note was added", while the notes kept accumulating. The model kept being re-woken (or never ended its turn) after an accepted declaration.

The wake source is not identified. Candidates:

- Muse's end-of-turn reminder or background-wake behaviour (see the related, superseded `sase-16i` and epic `sase-177`, "Muse single-turn normalization");
- a SASE nudge;
- a model self-loop.

The provider teardown watchdog (`start_completion_watchdog`, `src/sase/llm_provider/_subprocess_plain.py`) did not reap the run, presumably because the stream was never idle.

To reproduce, run a Muse phase agent whose bead legitimately cannot close yet (it is waiting on an unlanded host commit or a human gate). Watch `final_submission_attempts.jsonl` and the bead's notes after its first accepted `bead_action: keep` declaration.

issue.creation_reason: The sase-1my land agent found a Muse phase agent that kept looping after an accepted final declaration. It burned ~20 minutes of provider time and flooded its bead with 22 duplicate notes. This violates the single-turn contract and recurs for any Muse phase that cannot close in-turn.

payload.description: Earlier Muse post-declaration lifecycle bug (watchdog reaped waiting Muse runs); superseded by epic sase-177 whose single-turn normalization this loop escaped
The looping run; notes #5-#26 are the duplicate rechecks
